answers.rationale: For conference-style agendas, Tessa has accepted an official/on-site hotel without included breakfast when proximity to the meeting flow was the stronger operational benefit. A is also cheaper than D and provides the shortest indoor convention-center route. With both leading holds refundable, D's one-day-later deadline and included breakfast are secondary to A's location advantage.

C eliminates repeated transitions for Monday programming, the Monday reception, and Tuesday sessions. Tessa has prioritized official, adjacent conference lodging when it is reimbursable and meeting access is the central trip constraint, accepting no included breakfast and handling that separately. The $18 premium over Hampton is modest for being in the workshop building.

D meets the one-connection and coach requirements, has normal seat selection, is the lowest fare, leaves earliest after the stated midday cutoff, and returns latest after the closing lunch. Tessa treats carrier preference as secondary to schedule, connection quality, and seat-selection flexibility; the older Southwest family itinerary does not establish a work-trip Southwest preference.

B is the earliest-arriving nonstop and creates the most disruption buffer before the workshop for only a small premium over the later nonstop and cheaper one-stop options. Because no Salt Lake departure window is specified, the 8:40 a.m. departure is not disqualified. The hotel late-arrival note makes D viable, but does not outweigh B's substantially stronger arrival buffer.
